newsitem.title: DUBAI: BankWatch rates three Kuwaiti, one Omani bank.
newsitem.headline: BankWatch rates three Kuwaiti, one Omani bank.

text.p: U.S. rating agency Thomson BankWatch said on Tuesday it assigned ratings to one Oman-based and three Kuwaiti banks.
BankWatch said it assigned the Oman-based Bank of Oman, Bahrain and Kuwait an intra-country issuer rating of IC-B/C and a short-term local currency debt rating of LC-1.
"The bank has a long history of sound financial performance as evidenced by 22 years of consecutive dividend payments to shareholders," said a statement faxed to Reuters.

BankWatch said it had assigned the Kuwait-based Gulf Bank an intra-country issuer rating of IC-B and a short-term local currency debt rating of LC-1. Gulf Bank is the second largest of Kuwait's six commercial banks.

"Double-digit loan growth in 1996 and 1H 97 reflected a wide array of domestic lending...Liquidity remains solid despite the loan growth," the statement quoted BankWatch vice president William Hassiepen as saying. "The bank has an excellent equity base as well."
The rating agency assigned Al-Ahli Bank of Kuwait an intra-country issuer rating of IC-C and a short-term local currency debt rating of LC-1.

"Al-Ahli Bank of Kuwait's reputation in the past has been that of a troubled bank suffering from asset quality problems as well as difficulties with management," BankWatch said, but added that the bank was "at a turning point".

"While there are signs of a somewhat improving domestic market, it still has yet to see the growth and the dynamics of the market prior to August 1990. Opportunities do exist, however there is extremely stiff competition," it said.
BankWatch affirmed the Bank of Kuwait and the Middle East's intra-country issuer rating of IC-B/C and its short-term local currency debt rating of LC-1.

"Bank of Kuwait and the Middle East continues to progress favourably," the rating agency said. "While the bank continues to show improved performance, the increases in profitability are somewhat distorted due to non-recurring capital gains."
"The bank has moved into a stronger position within its rating category," BankWatch's Hassiepen said.
